analysis.title: Complicated picture
key_insights: TTF European natural gas surged past EUR100/MWh for the first time since the 2022 energy crisis, driven by escalating geopolitical tensions in Iran that threaten regional supply chains, one day before the ECB policy decision.

The energy spike compounds Eurozone inflation concerns and complicates the duration outlook. EUR rates face modest near-term headwinds while markets await the ECB decision, where no rate hike is expected.
Surging energy costs keep inflation upside risks intact, while growth headwinds and rising sovereign spreads temper near-term rate hike expectations.
Questions or references to EGB spreads will get the most scrutiny at the ECB meeting and Q&A. OAT valuations remain under scrutiny and keep elevated beta.

French Finance Minister Roland Lescure signalled the government will use all available tools on the budget, including article 49.3 or a 'Budget d'ordonnance'. The headline tightened OAT spreads versus Bunds intraday.
The October FOMC held the policy rate in a 3.75-4.00% target range with no surprises. The Treasury curve steepened as investors read Fed Chair Warsh's comments as dovish.
Markets price a 21bp Fed hike premium for the December meeting and 47bp through next March, roughly in line with the bank's house view of two 25bp hikes by March.
